title: Remove the redundant discarded-manager JWKS refresh
objective: Restore the documented one bounded unknown-kid refresh cycle by removing the redundant RequestRefresh call on a ConfigurationManager that is immediately discarded, without changing JWT trust policy or OAuth Desktop behavior.

included: Remove only the RequestRefresh invocation on the old ConfigurationManager immediately before replacement with a fresh manager.
Keep the refresh lock, pinned issuer/metadata/JWKS addresses, RS256/ES256 allow-list, issuer/audience/lifetime/subject/role checks and fail-closed result unchanged.
Retain per-path metadata and JWKS request counters proving exactly one initial fetch and one bounded unknown-kid refresh.
Focused backend test, complete Release verification and security review.
excluded: Any Supabase, Google, network, deployment, secret, token, .env, Git or live-smoke operation.
Changing JWT acceptance, retry counts elsewhere, cache intervals, endpoint derivation, HTTP transport, packages or Desktop authentication.
Accepting six requests, weakening the exact bound, or hiding the extra cycle in the test.

acceptanceCriteria: An unknown kid performs two metadata requests and two JWKS requests total: one initial cycle and one explicit refresh cycle.
The token remains Invalid after the refreshed JWKS still lacks the kid.
No trust, algorithm, issuer, audience, lifetime, subject or role validation changes.
Focused backend test, Release build and complete suite pass.
evidence: Full suite observed six total requests instead of four.
Per-path instrumentation observed three metadata requests where two are required.
SupabaseJwtValidator.RefreshAndValidateAsync calls RequestRefresh on the old manager and immediately replaces that manager before validation.
rollbackPlan: Restore the single removed RequestRefresh invocation if focused verification reveals a security regression.
Do not weaken tests or change external configuration.
